learning_objective: 🎯 Become a business optimizer! Learn how to maximize profits or minimize costs using graphs and mathematical constraints.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of your problem. Usually denoted as 'Z', it represents the profit you want to maximize or the cost you want to minimize, like $Z = 50x + 30y$.
In real life, resources aren't infinite. Constraints are inequalities representing your limits (like maximum budget, limited raw materials, or machine hours available).
When you graph all your constraints (inequalities) on paper, they overlap to form a shaded polygon. Every point inside this shaded shape is a 'valid' solution that obeys all rules.
You don't need to check all million points in the shaded region! The absolute maximum or minimum profit will ALWAYS happen at one of the sharp corners (vertices) of the feasible region.

fun_activity.title: 🧁 The Bakery Boss
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you run a bakery. Chocolate cakes give $10 profit but need 2 cups of sugar. Vanilla cakes give $8 profit but need 1 cup of sugar. If you only have 20 cups of sugar total, how many of each should you bake to get the most money? That's an LPP!

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw neatly using a scale and a pencil. Clearly shade the feasible region and write the coordinates of EVERY corner point on the graph.
📌 Do not forget the non-negativity constraints ($x \geq 0, y \geq 0$). They just mean you are operating entirely in the First Quadrant.
📌 If the feasible region is 'Unbounded' (open on one side), you MUST draw a dotted line for the objective function to verify if the optimal value is valid.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Objective Function is what you want to maximize (profit) or minimize (cost).
⭐ The overlapping shaded area is the Feasible Region.
⭐ The optimal answer always lives at a corner point.
